title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents via Harness-Policy Optimization
data_curation: The training set follows Orchard: 2,484 Python SWE tasks drawn from SWE-rebench, SWE-rebench V2 and Scale-SWE, shared between harness search and RL. The executable verifier gives binary rewards y(x, tau) in {0, 1}. The initial harness search set S0 is 300 tasks sampled at random from that set. Each later search set S_{t+1} is the set of hard tasks never resolved in any rollout during the preceding P-step; these are re-run with the updated harness and policy pair to produce fresh failure evidence. Inside an H-step, the proposer may read reference fixes for search-set tasks to compute diagnostics (coverage gap, precision gap, submission loss, fix archetypes), but it may not inject reference patches or task-specific facts into the harness. The SFT baseline uses only resolved Opus 4.8 trajectories on the same tasks.
curriculum: Self-HPO alternates H-steps (harness search with the policy frozen) and P-steps (RL with the harness frozen), following the schedule Base -> H1 -> P1 -> H2 -> P2. It stops when the hard-task set stabilizes, which happened after two rounds. Each H-step evaluates K=6 candidates once per search task, each revising the current best harness from all accumulated experience. Each P-step runs 50 RL updates starting from the previous policy. The evolving hard-task search set acts as an adaptive curriculum for harness search: it keeps the search pointed at the updated policy's failures. Freezing the initial search set instead costs 1.5 points (71.6 -> 70.1).
method: The base policy is Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and the seed harness is mini-SWE-agent; RL runs in slime on 8xB200 with SGLang serving. H-step: the current policy itself acts as a shell-access coding agent that analyzes failed trajectories and adds exactly one runtime mechanism per candidate. A candidate is a Python subclass that may override step() to inspect state, hold submissions or replace patches. The highest-scoring candidate on S_t becomes H_{t+1}. P-step: GRPO with Balanced Adaptive Rollout (BAR), which draws 8 rollouts per task and selects 4 to form reward-balanced groups with a success fraction of 0.25-0.75, until 32 groups yield 128 trajectories. The policy uses a token-level clipped objective (eps_low 0.2, eps_high 0.28), Adam at constant LR 1e-6, weight decay 0.01, entropy coefficient 1e-4, no KL penalty, and T = top-p = 0.95. The HPO variant swaps in Opus 4.8 as an external proposer. The evolved harness adds a budget valve, an empty-patch guard (git add -N), a one-time API-contract grounding check and a git-diff patch fallback.
eval_metrics: Benchmarks are SWE-Bench Verified (500 tasks, primary), SWE-Bench Multilingual (300 tasks, OOD) and SWE-Bench Pro public V2 (642 tasks, OOD). The metric is resolve rate avg@3 with std, using a 250-step limit and T = top-p = 0.95. Self-improving setup (Verified / Multilingual / Pro / avg): Base 61.0/54.2/58.3/57.8; RLVR 67.5/56.3/61.8/61.9; Self-Harness 65.2/54.3/60.7/60.1; Self-HPO 69.5/59.7/65.2/64.8. External Opus 4.8 setup: SFT 65.0/49.6/49.1/54.6; Meta-Harness 69.1/56.5/64.8/63.5; HPO 71.6/61.4/66.0/66.3. Pass@k on Verified (8 attempts): pass@8 rises from 80.0 to 84.8, and pass@1 improves +17.2/+12.9/+6.1 on Medium/Easy/Hard tasks but -2.2 on already-Resolved tasks. Zero-success RL groups fall to 6.5%, vs 11-17% for RLVR.
key_results: Self-HPO lifts Qwen3.5-35B-A3B's average resolve rate across the three SWE benchmarks from 57.8% to 64.8% (Verified 61.0 -> 69.5), beating RLVR by 2.9 and Self-Harness by 4.7 points on average. With Opus 4.8 as harness proposer, HPO reaches 71.6% on Verified. Cross-evaluation shows the evolved harness alone gives +3.5 and the trained policy alone +3.4, while the joint pair gives +8.5, more than the sum of the two.
evolution_note: Self-HPO joins two lines that had been developed separately: harness optimization with a frozen policy (Meta-Harness, Self-Harness, ADAS-style search) and policy RL under a fixed harness (GRPO/RLVR, Orchard's BAR, SWE-RL-style agents). Unlike concurrent joint methods (WHALE with a frozen external proposer, Evo2 with a separate trained proposer, HASE with harness edits inside the RL action space), it makes the RL-trained policy its own next harness proposer and derives the harness search set from tasks the RL step left unsolved. It also finds that improving the harness with a strong teacher beats SFT distillation from that same teacher, especially out of distribution.
